title: Normalize migration paths so migrate --undo detects symlinks
description: Normalize symlink target paths before migrated_tools() compares them. First-run migration can persist a relative .ddl target while later discovery computes an absolute path, so migrate --undo silently detects no migrated tools. This ticket covers detection only; existing DDL-el9 and DDL-cbp own single-file link creation and restoration.
acceptance_criteria: A failing regression test first creates a migrated directory config, reconstructs DdlDir in a separate invocation, and shows undo detection fails across relative/absolute path forms. Path comparison is normalized and migrate --undo detects the entry. Single-file restoration behavior is explicitly outside this ticket.
notes: Source: ../reports/round3-2026-08-04/VALIDATION-NOTES.md — dulce-de-leche B4. Related: DDL-el9, DDL-cbp. Verification: cargo test --test migrate.
close_reason: Fixed: migrated_tools resolves relative symlink targets to absolute and canonicalizes both resolved and expected paths before comparing, handling both directory and single-file symlink patterns.

title: P0: Add behavioral guardrails to AGENTS.md — Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers
description:
## Finding (from Agent Value Alignment audit)

AGENTS.md provides workflow instructions (wai → beads → openspec, TDD, session discipline) but **no behavioral guardrails**. An AI assistant working on this repo has no guidance on what it should/shouldn't do beyond the workflow.

### What's missing

- **Goal Sandwich**: The primary objective must appear verbatim at top AND bottom of the prompt (lost-in-the-middle countermeasure)
- **Prohibited behaviors (negations)**: 5 explicit "DON'T:" statements — e.g., DON'T make breaking changes without an openspec proposal, DON'T skip tests, DON'T refactor without test coverage
- **Escalation triggers**: The 7 named types — when to stop and ask (uncertainty, scope boundary, resource limit, anomaly detection, human review trigger, conflicting instructions, high stakes)
- **Minimal Footprint clause**: Resource/side-effect constraints for the assistant
- **Drift detection**: Self-check loop (ALIGNMENT check before major actions)

Your AGENTS.md is the strongest in the suite (context boundary warning, autonomous work policy) — but still missing: Goal Sandwich, explicit prohibitions, 7 escalation triggers, Minimal Footprint clause.

### What to do

1. Add a Goal Sandwich: objective statement in first 5 lines AND last 5 lines of the AGENTS.md prompt area
2. Add a "## Prohibited" section with 5+ explicit DON'T statements
3. Add a "## Stop and Ask" section with escalation triggers
4. Add a "## Minimal Footprint" clause
5. If eval tests exist, add a note about behavioral regression; if not, file a follow-up

### Priority rationale (P0)

Without behavioral guardrails, assistant behavior is unconstrained — the most common failure mode for AI-assisted development is scope creep and silent drift.

### References
- agent-value-alignment skill: references/layer-3-runtime-prompt.md
- Full audit report: genesis-ntg (genesis repo)
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-31: Added Goal Sandwich with ddl-specific objective, Prohibited section (6 DONTs including cross-platform verification requirement), Stop and Ask (7 triggers replacing the old 6-item list), Minimal Footprint, Drift Detection.
RO5 FIXES applied: moved guardrails outside WAI block (persistent across wai init), fixed echo consistency, reordered prohibitions by impact, sharpened scope/ambiguity triggers, made 400-line rule binary, added 3-approach limit to test failures, clarified rollback to git commands, readded autonomy policy lead-in. Also fixed wai-specific: removed .wai/projects/ from prohibited artifacts. Fixed dulce-de-leche: replaced unverifiable cross-compilation DON'T. Fixed espectacular: added DON'T about parallel genesis types. Fixed dont: added genesis donor note.
close_reason: Already addressed in commit 0f2482c — AGENTS.md now has behavioral guardrails including Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers, Minimal Footprint, and Drift Detection.

title: `migrate --undo` creates directory instead of file for single-file configs
description:
**File:** `src/dot_ddl.rs:unmigrate_tool()`

`create_dir_all(legacy_path)` when `legacy_path` was originally a file creates a
directory named `.pretender.toml`.

**Fix:** Detect the original type (file vs dir) before undo; for single-file
configs, move the file directly to `legacy_path` without `create_dir_all`.
notes: Co-modifies src/dot_ddl.rs with 5 other eval ticket(s): DDL-cbp, DDL-el9, DDL-40e, DDL-npg, DDL-sl0, DDL-ttg. Coordinate/rebase if picking up in parallel.
close_reason: Fixed: unmigrate_tool checks the symlink target type (file vs directory) before removing it, restoring single-file configs as files and directory configs as directories.

title: `migrate` corrupts single-file configs (`.pretender.toml`)
description:
**File:** `src/dot_ddl.rs:migrate_tool()`

When `legacy_path.is_file()`, the symlink is created pointing to the directory
(`.ddl/pretender/`) instead of the file, corrupting the config.

**Fix:**
```rust
// CORRECT (for file migration):
std::os::unix::fs::symlink(
    ddl_tool_path.join(legacy_path.file_name().unwrap_or_default()),
    legacy_path,
)
```
notes: Co-modifies src/dot_ddl.rs with 5 other eval ticket(s): DDL-cbp, DDL-el9, DDL-40e, DDL-npg, DDL-sl0, DDL-ttg. Coordinate/rebase if picking up in parallel.
close_reason: Fixed: migrate now creates symlink to the file inside .ddl/<tool>/ for single-file configs, not the directory. Also fixed unmigrate to detect single-file configs by checking symlink target type before removal.

title: Prevent concurrent manifest updates from losing entries
description: Round 3 review found that manifest mutations use an unsynchronized read-modify-write sequence. Parallel installs can each read the old manifest and overwrite the other entry.
acceptance_criteria: A concurrency regression test first reproduces lost updates. Manifest mutation becomes atomic or locked, and parallel installs preserve every successfully installed tool entry.
notes: Source: ../reports/round3-2026-08-04/backlogs/dulce-de-leche__sonnet-5.md — B7. Verification: cargo test --test manifest_concurrency.
close_reason: Fixed: record_tool and save_manifest now use advisory file locking (fs2) to serialize concurrent manifest read-modify-write cycles. The lock is acquired before re-reading the manifest from disk, ensuring the latest state is always used.

title: `migrate` is not idempotent
